Sees that the first pawn move and the kings' positions can matter more than the count

steps.text:
A **pawn majority** is more pawns than the opponent on one wing (files a-d or e-h). Its job is to make a **passed pawn**. The pawn with no enemy pawn in front of it on its own file is the **candidate**; it usually leads and the others follow.
Only *healthy* pawns count: no tactics, no doubled or blocked pawns.

steps.caption: White has two pawns against one on the queenside. White to move.

line.say: The a-pawn has no Black pawn in front of it. It leads and offers an exchange.
Black takes on a6. Each side now has one pawn on the wing.
White recaptures. Black has no pawns left, so the pawn on a6 is passed.

claims.statement: White wins from the start position (tablebase, exact).
After Black takes, each side has one pawn on the queenside.
After White recaptures, Black has no pawns on the queenside.
After White recaptures, Black has no pawns on the kingside either.
After the exchange the pawn on a6 is passed.

steps.text:
**Rule of thumb:** the candidate leads, the middle pawn waits. It holds only while the majority is healthy and nothing else interferes. Counting is the first step, not the last: **king position and tempo can decide**.
Next: three pawns against two, the Black king far away, and two different first moves.

steps.title: Same pawns, a different first move
steps.prompt: Now White plays the middle pawn two squares, b4, instead of a4. Predict the result first, then check.
Which part is least clear: counting the majority, choosing the candidate, or seeing when the kings matter more than the count?

steps.text: **Remember.** A pawn majority is more pawns on one wing, and its job is to make a passed pawn. The candidate, the pawn with no enemy pawn in front of it, leads and the middle pawn waits. It fails when the pawns are doubled, blocked or hit by tactics, and king position and tempo can decide.
